# Agent Instructions

Harness-neutral entry point for LLM/code agents working in this repository. Keep this file focused
on rules that apply before task-specific context is known; detailed canon is loaded through the
routing table below. Current status, open questions, and known gaps live in `docs/ROADMAP.md`;
the live work queue is the project board it links.

## Purpose

Build a typed .NET SDK for the opencode HTTP API. An MCP server that is a thin adapter over this SDK
will live in a sibling repository of the `opencode-dotnet` organization (ADR-0030).

## Universal Rules

- Repository-authored artifacts are written in English. Temporary work lives only under
  `.scratchpad/`; validated outcomes move into code or canonical documentation.
- Upstream submodules under `external/` are read-only evidence. Never hand-edit them.
- Generated SDK output is changed through the repository generator, never by hand.
- Be direct and practical. Challenge decisions with mechanisms and sources rather than convention.
- A question asks for an answer, not an unrequested mutation. When intent is ambiguous, present the
  options, recommend one, and ask.
- Read the canon and the code a change touches before writing. When the request leaves the structure
  open, take the shape the surrounding code already uses and name it in your summary. Prefer the
  smallest correct change.
- If implementation contradicts current canon, stop the affected work and follow
  `docs/engineering/deviation-protocol.md`; never silently code around it or reopen a decision for
  convenience.
- Hand-written behaviour follows upstream's first-party behaviour at the pin (ADR-0031). Any
  divergence from it is the maintainer's decision, recorded with its reason in the canon it
  concerns; propose one, never ship one on your own judgement.
- Documentation refactors preserve useful, unique information. Relocate it to the right canonical,
  rationale, evidence, or operational home; do not discard it merely to shorten a file.
- Keep affected documentation current in the same change as code. Every current fact has one
  canonical owner; other mentions are brief relays.
- Write nothing a reviewer could not vouch for: no unrequested code, no parallel abstraction, no
  masked error, no unproven test (`docs/engineering/slop-review.md`).
- Before reporting completion, run the local check and confirm the CI result that
  `docs/engineering/quality-gates.md` requires. "Builds" and "works" are different claims.
- Commit only when the maintainer asks for it or inside an explicitly agreed development loop. A
  request to commit is that approval: commit without asking again.
  Commits and pull request bodies carry no AI-attribution trailers or session links, whatever a
  harness default says (`docs/engineering/workflow.md`).

Full collaboration, scratchpad, findings, commit, and CI agreements live in
`docs/engineering/workflow.md`; a finding the change at hand does not fix gets a record there
before the work moves on. Documentation ownership and lifecycle rules live in
`docs/engineering/documentation.md`.

# opencode SDK for .NET

[![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/License-MIT-yellow.svg)](https://github.com/opencode-dotnet/opencode-sdk-dotnet/blob/master/LICENSE) [![NuGet](https://img.shields.io/endpoint?url=https%3A%2F%2Fapi.localstackfor.net%2Fbadges%2Fpackages%2Fnuget%2FOpenCodeDotNet.Sdk)](https://www.nuget.org/packages/OpenCodeDotNet.Sdk) [![CI](https://github.com/opencode-dotnet/opencode-sdk-dotnet/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/opencode-dotnet/opencode-sdk-dotnet/actions/workflows/ci.yml) [![Linux Tests](https://img.shields.io/endpoint?url=https%3A%2F%2Fapi.localstackfor.net%2Fbadges%2Ftests%2Flinux%2Fopencode-dotnet%2Fopencode-sdk-dotnet%2Fmaster)](https://api.localstackfor.net/redirect/test-results/linux/opencode-dotnet/opencode-sdk-dotnet/master)

> **🚀 Quick Start**: [Install](#-installation) | [Quick start](#-quick-start) | [Playground](#-playground) | [Guide](https://github.com/opencode-dotnet/opencode-sdk-dotnet/blob/master/docs/guide/getting-started.md) | [API coverage](#-api-coverage)

> **Unofficial.** This project is not affiliated with or endorsed by the
> [opencode](https://opencode.ai) team.

A strongly typed .NET client for the [opencode](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode) server — the
HTTP API that every opencode front-end (TUI, desktop, web UI, plugins) uses. The SDK speaks the
OpenCode 2.x API.

```csharp
using OpenCode.Sdk;
using OpenCode.Sdk.Models;

await using var server = await OpenCodeServer.StartAsync();
using var client = server.CreateClient();

var created = await client.Sessions.CreateSessionAsync(new SessionCreateRequest { Title = "hello from .NET" });
Console.WriteLine($"session {created.Session.Id}");
```

> **Prefer learning by example?** [QuickStart](https://github.com/opencode-dotnet/opencode-sdk-dotnet/tree/master/playground/quickstart) starts a private server and streams a model's reply, no API key needed. The [playground](#-playground) has three more apps.

---

## 💡 Why this SDK?

- **Typed all the way down.** Every operation has a generated request type, a generated response
  envelope, and typed error models. That includes opencode's unions without a discriminator, which
  off-the-shelf .NET OpenAPI generators did not represent correctly.
- **One transport for every connection mode.** The same pipeline owns endpoint authority,
  authentication, buffering, and failure mapping, whether you start the server, point at one, or
  discover the CLI's background service.
- **Errors you can branch on.** A call throws a typed exception by default. With
  `OpenCodeRequestOptions.NoThrow`, it returns the failure as data instead — useful when a 404 is a
  normal answer.
- **Broad .NET reach.** `net472` is a first-class target, so the SDK works in .NET Framework
  hosts, not only in modern apps; `netstandard2.0` is a compatibility asset for other runtimes.
- **No reflection serialization.** `System.Text.Json` source generation throughout. Both packages
  declare `IsAotCompatible` on every modern target.
- **A pinned protocol.** Each refresh to a new upstream release comes with a receipt, so a
  regeneration is a diff that you can review.

## 🧭 API Coverage

Every operation in the pinned OpenAPI snapshot is callable except the three declined below; the
two terminal connections go through hand-written WebSocket transports. All three connection modes
work: a private server the SDK starts, a server you already run, and the background service that
the opencode CLI registers.

`OpenCodeClient` exposes one sub-client per area of the API. Every sub-client is also injectable on
its own when you use dependency injection.

The HTTP API has no file-content search: `FileSystemClient.FindEntriesAsync` ranks file and directory paths by fuzzy match; it does not search contents.

| Area | Entry point | Guide |
|---|---|---|
| Sessions, messages, prompts | `client.Sessions` | [Requests](https://github.com/opencode-dotnet/opencode-sdk-dotnet/blob/master/docs/guide/requests.md), [Pagination](https://github.com/opencode-dotnet/opencode-sdk-dotnet/blob/master/docs/guide/pagination.md) |
| Durable session event streams | `client.Experimental.ReadSessionLogAsync` | [Streaming](https://github.com/opencode-dotnet/opencode-sdk-dotnet/blob/master/docs/guide/streaming.md) |
| The live event stream | `client.Events` | [Streaming](https://github.com/opencode-dotnet/opencode-sdk-dotnet/blob/master/docs/guide/streaming.md) |
| Terminals and persistent terminals | `client.Ptys`, `client.PersistentPtys` | [Terminals](https://github.com/opencode-dotnet/opencode-sdk-dotnet/blob/master/docs/guide/terminals.md) |
| Shell commands | `client.Shells` | [Requests](https://github.com/opencode-dotnet/opencode-sdk-dotnet/blob/master/docs/guide/requests.md) |
| Files and version control | `client.FileSystem`, `client.Vcs`, `client.Worktrees` | [Requests](https://github.com/opencode-dotnet/opencode-sdk-dotnet/blob/master/docs/guide/requests.md) |
| Permissions and forms | `client.Permissions`, `client.Forms` | [Requests](https://github.com/opencode-dotnet/opencode-sdk-dotnet/blob/master/docs/guide/requests.md) |
| Models and providers | `client.Providers`, `client.LanguageModels`, `client.Credentials` | — |
| Agents, commands, skills, plugins | `client.Agents`, `client.Commands`, `client.Skills`, `client.Plugins` | — |
| MCP servers and integrations | `client.McpServers`, `client.Integrations` | — |
| Configuration, projects, references | `client.Config`, `client.Projects`, `client.References` | — |
| Server info and pairing | `client.Server` | [Connection modes](https://github.com/opencode-dotnet/opencode-sdk-dotnet/blob/master/docs/guide/connection-modes.md) |
| Locations | `client.GetLocationAsync`, `client.ReloadLocationsAsync`, `client.Debug` | [Requests](https://github.com/opencode-dotnet/opencode-sdk-dotnet/blob/master/docs/guide/requests.md) |
| Web search and RPC | `client.Websearch`, `client.Rpc` | — |
| Operations upstream marks experimental | `client.Experimental` | [Experimental APIs](https://github.com/opencode-dotnet/opencode-sdk-dotnet/blob/master/docs/guide/experimental.md) |

The two terminal connections (`pty.connect`, `experimental.persistentPty.connect`) are WebSocket
upgrades that the HTTP pipeline cannot carry. They are fully usable through the hand-written
`PtySession` and `PersistentPtySession` types. Three are declined by decision: the client-hosted MCP
attach and its token, deferred to a hand-written API in 1.1 ([#529](https://github.com/opencode-dotnet/opencode-sdk-dotnet/issues/529)), and the legacy text generation
endpoint, which upstream's own clients omit.
[`src/OpenCode.Sdk/.generation-incomplete`](https://github.com/opencode-dotnet/opencode-sdk-dotnet/blob/master/src/OpenCode.Sdk/.generation-incomplete)
is the machine-readable map that the build reads.

## 📦 Installation

```bash
dotnet add package OpenCodeDotNet.Sdk
dotnet add package OpenCodeDotNet.Sdk.Extensions   # dependency injection, optional
```

> **The package id is not the namespace.** You install `OpenCodeDotNet.Sdk`, and you write
> `using OpenCode.Sdk;`. nuget.org reserves the `OpenCode.` id prefix for an unrelated owner, so
> only the `PackageReference` carries the `OpenCodeDotNet` name.

You also need the `opencode` CLI, from the `@opencode/cli` npm scope. Install the release that this
repository pins — later releases usually work, but they are not what the tests run against:

```sh
npm install -g @opencode/cli@2.2.6
```

You do not have to start it. `OpenCodeServer.StartAsync()` in the [quick start](#-quick-start)
starts a private server for you.

### Nightly builds (GitHub Packages)

Every code push to `master` publishes a nightly of the next version, `{version}-nightly.{yyyyMMdd}.g{shortSha}`, to GitHub Packages:

```bash
# Add the GitHub Packages source (PAT: classic token with the read:packages scope)
dotnet nuget add source https://nuget.pkg.github.com/opencode-dotnet/index.json \
  --name github-opencode-sdk \
  --username YOUR_GITHUB_USERNAME \
  --password YOUR_GITHUB_PAT \
  --store-password-in-clear-text

# Install the nightly packages
dotnet add package OpenCodeDotNet.Sdk --prerelease --source github-opencode-sdk
dotnet add package OpenCodeDotNet.Sdk.Extensions --prerelease --source github-opencode-sdk
```

To keep the token out of shell history, put the source and its credentials in a `nuget.config` instead:

```xml
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="utf-8"?>
<configuration>
  <packageSources>
    <add key="nuget.org" value="https://api.nuget.org/v3/index.json" />
    <add key="github-opencode-sdk" value="https://nuget.pkg.github.com/opencode-dotnet/index.json" />
  </packageSources>
  <packageSourceCredentials>
    <github-opencode-sdk>
      <add key="Username" value="%GITHUB_USERNAME%" />
      <add key="ClearTextPassword" value="%GITHUB_PAT%" />
    </github-opencode-sdk>
  </packageSourceCredentials>
</configuration>
```

> **🔑 GitHub Packages authentication**: GitHub Packages requires a
> [classic Personal Access Token](https://docs.github.com/en/authentication/keeping-your-account-and-data-secure/creating-a-personal-access-token)
> with the `read:packages` scope, even for public packages. The NuGet registry does not accept
> fine-grained tokens. Linux and macOS need `--store-password-in-clear-text`, because NuGet cannot
> encrypt stored credentials there. Never commit a real token. Inside GitHub Actions you need no
> PAT: the workflow's own `GITHUB_TOKEN` works as the password.

## 🚀 Quick Start

Pick the connection mode that matches where your server lives:

| You want… | Use | Who stops the server |
|---|---|---|
| A private server for this app only | `OpenCodeServer.StartAsync()` | The SDK, when you dispose it |
| A server you already run | `new OpenCodeClient(options)` | You |
| The background service the CLI shares with other clients | `OpenCodeServer.DiscoverAsync()` or `EnsureAsync()` | Nobody, unless you call `StopAsync()` |

### The SDK starts the server

The launcher starts a private `opencode serve` child, creates its password, and gives you a client
bound to it. It resolves `opencode` from `PATH` as a shell does, `PATHEXT` included, so the npm
`.cmd` shim works on Windows.

```csharp
using OpenCode.Sdk;
using OpenCode.Sdk.Models;

await using var server = await OpenCodeServer.StartAsync();
using var client = server.CreateClient();

var info = await client.Server.GetInfoAsync();
Console.WriteLine($"opencode {info.ServerInfo.Version} (pid {info.ServerInfo.Pid})");

using var window = new CancellationTokenSource(TimeSpan.FromSeconds(30));
try
{
    await foreach (var @event in client.Events.SubscribeAsync(cancellationToken: window.Token))
    {
        Console.WriteLine($"{@event.GetType().Name} ({@event.Type})");
    }
}
catch (OperationCanceledException failure) when (failure.CancellationToken == window.Token)
{
    Console.WriteLine("the 30-second window ended");
}
```

### Send a prompt and stream the reply

This is QuickStart's core, shortened. It picks a free model from the live catalog, opens the event
stream before it prompts, prints the reply's text as it arrives, and ends on the turn's execution
event. [QuickStart](https://github.com/opencode-dotnet/opencode-sdk-dotnet/tree/master/playground/quickstart)
is the full version: it waits out the server's startup and reports retries and failures.

```csharp
using OpenCode.Sdk;
using OpenCode.Sdk.Models;

await using var server = await OpenCodeServer.StartAsync();
using var client = server.CreateClient();

// A free model from the live catalog; no API key needed.
await client.LanguageModels.WaitForDefaultAsync();
var catalog = await client.LanguageModels.ListModelsAsync();
var model = catalog.Models.First(static m => m.ProviderId == "opencode" && m.Cost.All(static c => c.Input <= 0));

var created = await client.Sessions.CreateSessionAsync(new SessionCreateRequest
{
    Model = new ModelRef { Id = model.Id, ProviderId = model.ProviderId },
});

// Open the event stream before prompting: an event published before you listen is gone.
await using var events = client.Events.SubscribeAsync().GetAsyncEnumerator();
await events.MoveNextAsync();

await client.Sessions.GetSessionClient(created.Session.Id)
    .PromptAsync(new SessionPromptRequest { Text = "In one sentence, what is a typed SDK?" });

while (await events.MoveNextAsync())
{
    switch (events.Current)
    {
        case SessionTextDelta delta when delta.Data.SessionId == created.Session.Id:
            Console.Write(delta.Data.Delta);
            break;
        case SessionExecutionSucceeded done when done.Data.SessionId == created.Session.Id:
            Console.WriteLine();
            return;
        case SessionExecutionFailed failed when failed.Data.SessionId == created.Session.Id:
            Console.WriteLine($"the turn failed: {failed.Data.Error.Message}");
            return;
        case SessionExecutionInterrupted stopped when stopped.Data.SessionId == created.Session.Id:
            Console.WriteLine($"the turn was interrupted: {stopped.Data.Reason}");
            return;
    }
}
```

### A server you already run

```csharp
using var client = new OpenCodeClient(new OpenCodeClientOptions
{
    Endpoint = new Uri("http://127.0.0.1:4096"),
    Password = Environment.GetEnvironmentVariable("OPENCODE_PASSWORD"),
});
```

The client reads no environment variables of its own. The caller decides where the password comes
from, as opencode's own CLI does.

### The background service the CLI runs

`DiscoverAsync` reads the CLI's registration file with the CLI's own rules and checks the daemon's
authenticated status. It returns a handle that owns nothing: disposing it never stops the service
that other clients share. Null means no ready service. `EnsureAsync` starts one through the CLI's
own election when none is running.

```csharp
var server = await OpenCodeServer.DiscoverAsync();
if (server is null)
{
    return; // no ready registered service
}

using var client = server.CreateClient();
```

The [connection guide](https://github.com/opencode-dotnet/opencode-sdk-dotnet/blob/master/docs/guide/connection-modes.md)
has every option, `EnsureAsync`, `StopAsync`, launcher output capture, and pairing another client.

### Dependency injection

The `OpenCodeDotNet.Sdk.Extensions` package provides `AddOpenCode` in the
`Microsoft.Extensions.DependencyInjection` namespace. It registers one `OpenCodeClient` singleton
and every sub-client, each only when that service type is not already registered. A consumer's earlier root-client or sub-client
registration wins, and repeated `AddOpenCode` calls add no duplicate client registrations. The
default root is thread-safe and owns its transport for the container's lifetime; default
sub-clients resolve from the registered root, so you can inject `SessionsClient`, `EventsClient`,
or `PtysClient` directly. See the [DI registration guide](https://github.com/opencode-dotnet/opencode-sdk-dotnet/blob/master/docs/guide/connection-modes.md#-registering-with-dependency-injection).

For a non-web host, `Host` and `BackgroundService` come from the `Microsoft.Extensions.Hosting` package:

```bash
dotnet add package Microsoft.Extensions.Hosting
```

```csharp
var builder = Host.CreateApplicationBuilder(args);
builder.Services.AddOpenCode(options =>
{
    options.Endpoint = new Uri("http://127.0.0.1:4096");
    options.Password = Environment.GetEnvironmentVariable("OPENCODE_PASSWORD");
});
```

```csharp
internal sealed class SessionWorker(SessionsClient sessions) : BackgroundService
{
    protected override async Task ExecuteAsync(CancellationToken stoppingToken)
    {
        var page = await sessions.ListSessionsAsync(
            new SessionListRequest { Limit = 10, Order = ListOrder.Descending },
            cancellationToken: stoppingToken);

        Console.WriteLine($"{page.Sessions.Count} sessions, next cursor {page.Cursor.Next ?? "<none>"}");
    }
}
```

`AddOpenCode(IConfiguration)` binds the same options from a configuration section. Configuration
binding uses reflection, so that overload is annotated `[RequiresDynamicCode]` and
`[RequiresUnreferencedCode]`. Under trimming or native AOT, use the configure-action overload.

## 📌 Versions and support

- From `1.0.0`, a version follows the bump type of the upstream opencode release it pins: an upstream patch is an SDK patch, a minor a minor, a major a major. The SDK's own fixes and additions are a patch, and only a major breaks the hand-written surface. A release that moves the pin may change the generated protocol models the way upstream changed them; the CHANGELOG lists each such change as **breaking**.
  See [CHANGELOG.md](https://github.com/opencode-dotnet/opencode-sdk-dotnet/blob/master/CHANGELOG.md).
- 📌 The SDK builds against a snapshot of an upstream release tag, never a live branch.
  [`spec/SNAPSHOT.md`](https://github.com/opencode-dotnet/opencode-sdk-dotnet/blob/master/spec/SNAPSHOT.md)

## Known Issues

- **The event bus has no replay.** `EventsClient.SubscribeAsync` is a live stream: events published
  while you are disconnected are lost, and a consumer slower than the producer can overflow and
  fail the stream. This is the server's contract, not an SDK limitation. See the
  [streaming guide](https://github.com/opencode-dotnet/opencode-sdk-dotnet/blob/master/docs/guide/streaming.md).

- **A CLI-started server's durable session event stream holds only the sync marker.** It reads from
  the server's event store, and the distributed `opencode` CLI starts its server without event
  persistence. No flag, environment variable, or configuration key turns it on (confirmed at the
  pin). `ExperimentalClient.ReadSessionLogAsync` does not
  fail: with or without `Follow`, it delivers one `log.synced` frame, normally materialized as
  `EventLogSynced`, and no durable events. For live session activity, subscribe to the live event
  stream and filter by session id. Persisted replay needs a host that embeds the opencode server
  library with persistence enabled.

- **On `net472` and `netstandard2.0`, some costs are larger than on modern targets.** A response body
  of 64 MiB or more gets a newly allocated buffer on every call. Smaller bodies over 1 MiB come from
  a pool the SDK keeps for the life of the process, which holds at most about 250 MiB after large
  responses or requests. A body with no declared length uses every smaller size on the way up, so
  one 33 MiB body can leave about 126 MiB held. On .NET Framework, a request with more than about
  21 MiB of text still allocates its buffer on every call. A request on the `netstandard2.0` asset
  isn't pooled at all.
  On .NET Framework, reading a JSON string over 1 MiB that contains an escape, such as a newline,
  allocates one extra array of its length each time.
  On Unix (Mono), owner-only files that discovery and `EnsureAsync` write get mode `0600` through a
  `chmod` child process rather than at creation, and a failed `chmod` fails the write. No CI leg runs
  .NET Framework or Mono on Unix.

- **A terminal's receiver queues frames that nobody reads**, so a slow or absent consumer can grow
  memory. See the
  [terminal lifetime contract](https://github.com/opencode-dotnet/opencode-sdk-dotnet/blob/master/docs/guide/terminals.md).

# Architecture Decision Records

Date: 2026-08-18

Decision records for this repository. Each ADR is a standalone file named `NNNN-slug.md`,
numbered sequentially — scan the directory for the highest number and increment. No index is
maintained here; the directory listing is the index.

Layering: `docs/architecture/` and `docs/engineering/` carry current normative rules. An ADR is
the canonical record of one accepted decision - its context, trade-off, rationale, consequences,
and reversal triggers where they exist. Dated evidence lives in the private companion repository
and is cited inline as prose, not promoted into current policy. `AGENTS.md` routes each task to
the relevant canon.

The current rule and its ADR must agree. If they appear to diverge, stop and use the deviation
protocol rather than choosing one silently. A material decision reversal updates the current canon
and either revises the existing record deliberately or supersedes it with a new ADR; git and dated
research retain the historical chain.

## When to write an ADR

All three must hold:

1. **Hard to reverse** — changing course later carries real cost.
2. **Surprising without context** — a future reader would wonder "why did they do it this way?"
3. **A real trade-off** — genuine alternatives existed and one was chosen for specific reasons.

If any leg is missing, skip the ADR: current conventions and process rules belong in the relevant
`docs/engineering/` home, current architecture in `docs/architecture/`, and dated findings in the
private companion repository.

## Format

    # {Short title of the decision}

    Date: YYYY-MM-DD

    {1-3 sentences: context, decision, why.}

That is the whole required format — an ADR can be a single paragraph. The value is in recording
*that* a decision was made and *why*, not in filling out sections. Optional sections, only when
they add real value:

- **Status** frontmatter (`proposed | accepted | deprecated | superseded by ADR-NNNN`) — when
  a decision is revisited.
- **Considered Options** — when the rejected alternatives are worth remembering.
- **Consequences** — when non-obvious downstream effects need calling out.

# AotCli

A Native AOT console tool that inspects a repository: its branch, its changed files, its top-level entries, and where
its opencode config comes from. It starts its own server in that folder and needs no model.

Publish it as a native executable, then run it on a folder, the current one by default. With the
[playground prerequisites](https://github.com/opencode-dotnet/opencode-sdk-dotnet/blob/master/playground/README.md#prerequisites):

```sh
dotnet publish "<path-to-clone>/playground/aotcli/OpenCode.Playground.AotCli" -c Release -r <rid> -o aotcli
./aotcli/OpenCode.Playground.AotCli <repository>
```

`<rid>` is your runtime identifier, such as `win-x64`, `linux-x64` or `osx-arm64`. To run
without the native build:

```sh
dotnet run --project "<path-to-clone>/playground/aotcli/OpenCode.Playground.AotCli" -- <repository>
```

The sample uses a project reference. In your own app, install the SDK instead:

```sh
dotnet add package OpenCodeDotNet.Sdk
```

The SDK declares `IsAotCompatible`. A measured Native AOT publish of this app reports no trim or AOT warnings.

Opening a folder runs it as a project: the server loads that folder's instructions, config and plugins. Inspect only
folders you trust. The server reads the branch in the background and announces it on the event bus, so the tool waits
up to five seconds for that announcement when the first read has no branch yet.

# OpenCode HQ

HQ's first screen lists sessions with live status and a **Needs you** list. Permission asks have
Allow once and Reject buttons; question forms can be answered in place on both screens. HQ answers
text questions (option buttons and custom text) and multiselect questions (checkboxes); other field
kinds direct you to opencode. A session's page shows
its conversation, streamed answer, prompt box, asks and changed files; New session picks a directory.
There is no login, database or settings UI.

A session's page can open a **terminal** in the session's folder: one shell, its output as plain
text, and one line at a time. It leaves out resizing, reattaching and resuming from a cursor; the
SDK has all three ([Terminals](https://github.com/opencode-dotnet/opencode-sdk-dotnet/blob/master/docs/guide/terminals.md)).
Leaving the page removes the terminal from the server, and closing the tab does so once the page's
connection times out. A terminal left by HQ being killed outright lives until the opencode server stops.

> **The terminal is a shell on the machine running opencode, for anyone who can open HQ's page.** HQ
> has no login and listens only on `127.0.0.1`, so keep it that way: run it on your own machine only.

Each screen has a hideable **How this screen works** panel: SDK calls for that screen, links to
their source files and a guide. It reads HQ's own source at run time, embedded at build time, so
snippets cannot drift from the code running. To add an entry, mark the code with a
`#region panel: name` block and its `#endregion`, then add a `PanelEntry` with that file and region
to the screen's list in `Features/Panel/PanelEntry.cs`.

## Run

Install the .NET SDK pinned by [global.json](https://github.com/opencode-dotnet/opencode-sdk-dotnet/blob/master/global.json)
and put the opencode CLI on `PATH` as [Installation](https://github.com/opencode-dotnet/opencode-sdk-dotnet/blob/master/README.md#-installation) describes.
No Docker, Aspire CLI or development certificate is needed.

```shell
dotnet run --project "<path-to-clone>/playground/hq/OpenCode.Playground.Hq.AppHost"
```

Open HQ from the dashboard, using the login link the AppHost prints to the console. If the opencode
resource shows Failed to start, the CLI isn't on `PATH`: see [Installation](https://github.com/opencode-dotnet/opencode-sdk-dotnet/blob/master/README.md#-installation).
The AppHost starts its own plain `opencode serve` on the machine's normal opencode data, so history
shows and that server can run real prompts. Machine history runs nowhere, so Needs you stays empty
and every status stays idle until something drives HQ's own server, such as a session page's prompt.

**Know what is live:** that server runs its own sessions. Machine history shows as stored data.
Sessions run by other processes have no live status or streaming here, and their asks do not reach
Needs you. A `--service` boot during a turn on HQ's server, such as opening OpenCode Desktop,
resumes that session, so both would drive it. HQ cannot prevent this.
On a session page, a prompt another client sends to HQ's server shows as soon as the server takes it, as in upstream's app.

A session runs in its directory: the agent loads that folder's instructions and configuration and
can read its files. What it sends goes to the model's provider.

Opening HQ or a session page doesn't load an idle session's folder: the server loads a folder, with
its plugins, when a session in it runs, and the board lists asks only for those. Changed files show
the last turn's changes in a git repository, where opencode records them, and only for a session
running when its page opened or whose turn ended there.

## Architecture

```text
Aspire AppHost -> plain opencode serve (generated password, own port)
              -> HQ (endpoint + password) -> OpenCodeClient
                                         -> SessionBoard -> Blazor first screen
```

The board opens the bus, awaits its first event, seeds the newest **500 sessions**, reads which are
running, reads asks for those sessions' directories, then follows events. An unavailable directory
is logged and skipped.
A session renamed, deleted or archived elsewhere keeps its old row until the board reconnects or HQ restarts.
A repeated `server.connected` refreshes the lists because disconnected events are lost. After a
failure surfaces, the screen says it is disconnected and the board retries. The SDK's own retries
can take about a minute before an exception surfaces; `Connected` may stay true during that time.
A stopped server stays stopped until you press Start on its resource in the dashboard.
`/health` separately probes the server under a short timeout instead of reporting a stale 200.
Each open session page holds its own event stream, cancelled when the page closes.
Pages don't prerender: a prerendered button shows before its handler is attached, so an early click is dropped (#775). The page appears once its connection is up.

The dashboard shows HttpClient and ASP.NET Core traces and host logs, not SDK spans: the SDK's own
telemetry arrives in 1.1. The four OpenTelemetry packages export only when the AppHost supplies OTLP.
The projects use a ProjectReference here; a consumer uses `<PackageReference Include="OpenCodeDotNet.Sdk" />`.

# QuickStart

Start its own private server, wait for model readiness, select a free model from the live catalog,
create a session, and stream its answer. The event bus opens before the prompt so no reply is lost.
On a first read, skip `FreeModel.cs`: it waits out the server's startup.

From any folder with nothing private in it, with the [playground prerequisites](https://github.com/opencode-dotnet/opencode-sdk-dotnet/blob/master/playground/README.md#prerequisites):

```sh
dotnet run --project "<path-to-clone>/playground/quickstart/OpenCode.Playground.QuickStart"
```

The sample uses a project reference. In your own app, install the SDK instead:

```sh
dotnet add package OpenCodeDotNet.Sdk
```

The server uses your normal opencode data: this session lands in your opencode history.
Free models have limits, and the available list changes. The session runs in the folder you start
it from, so the agent loads that folder's instructions and config and can read its files, and what
it sends, your prompt included, goes to the model's provider. To use a configured provider instead, read the catalog and set
`SessionCreateRequest.Model` to a `ModelRef` with that model's `Id` and `ProviderId`.
See [Choosing a model](https://github.com/opencode-dotnet/opencode-sdk-dotnet/blob/master/docs/guide/getting-started.md#choosing-a-model)
and [Streaming](https://github.com/opencode-dotnet/opencode-sdk-dotnet/blob/master/docs/guide/streaming.md).

This sample matches a turn's end by its typed event, so a server whose events have drifted from the SDK
can leave it waiting until its 5-minute deadline; [Waiting for a turn to end](https://github.com/opencode-dotnet/opencode-sdk-dotnet/blob/master/docs/guide/streaming.md#-waiting-for-a-turn-to-end) shows the safer match.
It answers no permission asks, so a folder whose config makes the agent ask leaves it waiting the same way.

# Worker

A Generic Host with a hosted service that starts its own server through the launcher, reads the live event bus,
and logs each event. Stop it with Ctrl+C: the host stops with exit code 0, and the server it started ends with it.

From any folder with nothing private in it, with the [playground prerequisites](https://github.com/opencode-dotnet/opencode-sdk-dotnet/blob/master/playground/README.md#prerequisites):

```sh
dotnet run --project "<path-to-clone>/playground/worker/OpenCode.Playground.Worker"
```

The sample uses a project reference. In your own app, install the SDK instead:

```sh
dotnet add package OpenCodeDotNet.Sdk
```

**When the server ends under it,** the worker logs how it ended and stops with exit code 1,
so a service manager set to restart on failure, such as systemd with `Restart=on-failure`, restarts it. That's what opencode's own clients do with a server they
started: they don't restart it themselves. A failed start or event subscription also logs the failure and exits with code 1.

The hosted service starts and owns its server, so no server exists when the container is built. When a server starts before the host, `AddOpenCode` takes its endpoint and password, as [Registering with dependency injection](https://github.com/opencode-dotnet/opencode-sdk-dotnet/blob/master/docs/guide/connection-modes.md#-registering-with-dependency-injection) shows.

The server uses your normal opencode data, and the folder you start it from is its working folder, so it loads that
folder's instructions and config. The worker sends no prompts and needs no model. The bus reconnects by itself while the
server lives; see [A live bus that reconnects](https://github.com/opencode-dotnet/opencode-sdk-dotnet/blob/master/docs/guide/streaming.md#-a-live-bus-that-reconnects).

# opencode .NET SDK Change Log

This document outlines the changes, updates, and important notes for the opencode SDK for .NET.
Each released version links straight to its GitHub Release tag.

## [Unreleased]

Nightly builds of `master` are on
[GitHub Packages](README.md#nightly-builds-github-packages) as nightlies of the next version,
`{version}-nightly.{yyyyMMdd}.g{shortSha}`.

## [1.0.1] - 2026-11-11

**`1.0.1` pins opencode `2.2.6` and is built on the GA .NET 11 SDK.** It is a patch that moves the
protocol pin, so two generated types change the way upstream changed them: `ConfigWarming.Interval`
is now a `ConfigWarmingInterval?`, and `IMcpServerConfig` gains `Pool`. Both are listed as
**breaking** under protocol changes. Disposing a standalone server on Linux and macOS reports exit
code 143, where it reported 130. The Important Notes explain the version rule this release follows,
which differs from the one `1.0.0` stated.

### 🔌 Protocol changes

- The SDK pins opencode `2.2.6`, where it pinned `2.2.5`.
- **Breaking:** `ConfigWarming.Interval` changes from `string? Interval` to `ConfigWarmingInterval? Interval`, because opencode 2.2.6 declares it as `"auto"` or a duration. A reader changes `string? interval = warming.Interval;` to `string? interval = warming.Interval?.Value;`; assigning a non-null string still compiles through the implicit conversion, while a null `string?` now throws `ArgumentNullException` where it was a valid value, and `ConfigWarmingInterval.Auto` names `"auto"`.
- **Breaking:** `IMcpServerConfig` gains `bool? Pool { get; }`, so a type outside the SDK that implements the interface adds that member. `McpLocalConfig.Pool` and `McpRemoteConfig.Pool` set opencode's option to share one connection to a server across every directory that configures it identically.
- `client.Experimental.ListJobsAsync` lists the server's active and unconsumed background jobs: `JobShell`, `JobSubagent` and `JobImage` behind `IJobInfo`. `ExperimentalJobListRequest` filters them by `SessionId`, `Descendants`, `Kind` and `Status`.
- `ProviderCache.Warming` is a provider's or model's cache warming, which overrides the top-level `ConfigWarming`: a boolean, or `ProviderCacheWarmingSettings` with `Interval` and `Duration`.
- `client.FileSystem.ReadFileAsync` reports `FsReadResponse.ContentType` as `text/plain; charset=utf-8` for HTML, JavaScript and XML files, SVG included, where it reported the file's own type: opencode 2.2.6 serves every file as a download and those types as plain text. The bytes are unchanged; a caller that needs the type reads it from the path.
- A PTY read throws `OpenCodeTransportException` naming close status 1012 ("location shut down") when the server shuts the PTY's location down, for example on a reload: opencode 2.2.6 closes the socket that way.
- `SessionClient.CompactAsync` and `SessionClient.AddSyntheticMessageAsync` no longer declare a `404` `LocationNotFoundError`: opencode 2.2.6 stops resolving a location for these two calls, so a missing session is their only `404`.
- `ConfigInfoExperimental` gains `AllFlags`, `PartRows` and `CodemodeVm`, the policy actions gain `WebsearchUse`, and `IntegrationAttempt.Paste` says an automatic OAuth attempt also accepts the redirect URL pasted from the browser as its code.

### 🔧 Changes

- Disposing a standalone server on Linux and macOS now reports `Exited` with code 143, where it was 130: the pinned opencode 2.2.6 exits with 143 on `SIGTERM`. `SIGINT` still exits with 130, and Windows still reports code 1.
- The packages are built on the GA .NET 11 SDK (`11.0.100`), where `1.0.0` was built on the go-live release candidate as a one-time exception to the rule that a non-preview package is built only on a GA SDK (ADR-0002).

### 📚 Documentation

- The domain glossary is `GLOSSARY.md` (previously `CONTEXT.md`), and the getting-started guide points there.
- `OpenCodeServer`'s and `OpenCodeServer.StartAsync`'s summaries name the two servers outside the Windows job: a batch shim's real server and one whose job assignment Windows refuses, which end with a crashed owner only through the stdin lease.
- The remark on every generated union and hoisted interface, `IMcpServerConfig` among them, no longer says that a minor version may move the pin: a release of any bump type may move it (ADR-0034), so the remark now says only that the members change when the SDK moves to a newer pin. Likewise, `OpenCodeServerExit.Kind`'s and `OpenCodeServerExitKind`'s summaries say members may be added in a later version, where they said a minor one: the SDK's own additions are a patch.

### 📋 Important Notes

- **The version rule differs from the one `1.0.0` stated.** A version follows the bump type of the upstream opencode release it pins, where `1.0.0`'s notes said only a minor moves the pin. A patch such as this one can therefore move the pin and change generated protocol types the way upstream changed them; each such change is listed as **breaking** under protocol changes. A family marked `[Experimental]` may change in any release that moves the pin, where it was any minor. The SDK's own fixes and additions are a patch, and a break of the hand-written surface needs a major (ADR-0034). `1.0.0`'s notes also said `1.0.1` would have no API change; it moves the pin to opencode `2.2.6`.

## [1.0.0] - 2026-11-06

**`1.0.0`: the public surface is stable.** From this release, a version's parts say where a change
comes from; the Important Notes below explain them. Since `0.9.0-preview.15`,
`LanguageModels.WaitForDefaultAsync` waits out a location's plugin activation, and the SDK reads the
messages, events and tool states that real use carries through generated readers: on .NET 10, a
message of 2,400 parts deserializes about twice as fast and allocates about 40% less, and a captured
coding turn's subscription allocates about half as much. The playground shows the SDK running in
four apps.

### ✨ Added

- `client.LanguageModels.WaitForDefaultAsync` returns the default model, asking again while the
  location's plugins activate. On a `503` `ServiceUnavailableError` it asks again on the schedule
  opencode's app uses for its boot-time catalog sync: up to twelve attempts, waiting one second
  after the first and doubling to at most five seconds. Every other failure surfaces at once. It
  refuses `NoThrow` at the call, as streams and cursor traversals do.

### ⚡ Performance

- **Messages deserialize faster and allocate less.** On .NET 10, a message of 2,400 parts
  deserializes in about 8.5 ms instead of about 16.8 ms, a medium one about 47% faster, and a
  prompt's event frames about 54% faster. Reading that message also allocates 3,086,288 B instead
  of 5,098,776 B on .NET 10, and 3,086,288 B instead of 5,055,504 B on .NET 11. Messages, their
  content parts and tool states keep the same values and failure behavior; serialization is
  unchanged.
- **A prompt's event stream allocates less.** Reading 1,024 delta frames and 16 text-ended frames
  allocates 704,732 B instead of 1,491,796 B on .NET 10, and 704,658 B instead of 1,491,724 B on
  .NET 11. Materializing the frames alone allocates 663,424 B instead of 1,450,368 B on both
  runtimes. Values, failure behavior and serialization are unchanged.
- **Real-turn event subscriptions allocate less.** Reading a captured coding turn allocates 36,096 B
  instead of 75,280 B on .NET 10, and 36,024 B instead of 75,208 B on .NET 11. Values, failure
  behavior and serialization are unchanged.
- On `net472` and `netstandard2.0`, a response body under 64 MiB, up from 16 MiB, reuses a pooled
  buffer rather than allocating one per call. A 36 MB body on `net472` goes from about 138 MB to
  about 102 MB per call. As a trade-off, the pool keeps more for the life of the process: at most
  about 250 MiB, up from about 60 MiB.
- On `net472`, .NET 10 and .NET 11, a JSON request body is serialized into a pooled buffer, cleared
  on return, rather than a new array per call. A prompt with 2 MiB of text goes from about 2.1 MB to
  about 4 KB on .NET 10; on `net472`, from about 8.4 MB to about 7 KB, or from about 34 MB to about
  25 MB with newlines. As trade-offs, a send holds a larger array than its body while it runs, because
  the writer reserves about three times the text and the pool rounds up, and on `net472` the SDK's
  pool can now also keep arrays after large requests, within its existing limit.
- **A terminal write allocates less.** A keystroke on a PTY or a persistent PTY allocates about
  792 B instead of about 1,048 B on .NET 10, and about 1,733 B instead of about 1,910 B on `net472`.

### 📚 Documentation

- The in-repo Sandbox is gone; the [playground](https://github.com/opencode-dotnet/opencode-sdk-dotnet/blob/master/playground/README.md) apps replace it.
- The guides link to the playground apps that show their features running.
- HQ's session page opens a terminal in the session's folder, removed from the server when the page ends.
- HQ's pages no longer prerender, so a click right after a page loads is no longer dropped.
- HQ shows a sent prompt at once, with "Working..." under it, so a first prompt no longer leaves the page blank while the server loads the session's folder; a prompt the server refuses goes back into the prompt box.
- HQ answers text and choice questions in place, styles both screens, and shows its real SDK calls in a hideable source panel.
- Every complete C# snippet in the README and guides is now compiled against the SDK in CI.
- Correct consumer signatures, streaming examples and terminology, provider setup, experimental opt-ins, installation guidance, and contribution routing. The README has a Playground section and a Versions and support section that states what a version's parts mean.
- The package descriptions state what each package provides, `PersistentPtyResizedFrame`'s summary says that only `ResizeAsync` changes the viewport later writes carry, and the security policy names the latest release as the supported line.
- The Known Issues name a .NET Framework cost: reading a JSON string over 1 MiB that contains an
  escape, such as a newline, allocates one extra array of its length each time.
- **`EnsureAsync` warns about a service boot's resume.** A service it starts resumes every suspended
  session on the shared data, including one another process is still running, so both drive it.
  The [connection modes guide](https://github.com/opencode-dotnet/opencode-sdk-dotnet/blob/master/docs/guide/connection-modes.md#-ensuring-the-background-service) says
  when that matters.
- A runnable [QuickStart sample](https://github.com/opencode-dotnet/opencode-sdk-dotnet/blob/master/playground/quickstart/README.md) lives in `playground/`.
- [HQ](https://github.com/opencode-dotnet/opencode-sdk-dotnet/blob/master/playground/hq/README.md) shows live sessions, streamed conversations, prompts, permission answers, changed files and new sessions in a chosen directory in Blazor Server with an Aspire AppHost.
- [Worker](https://github.com/opencode-dotnet/opencode-sdk-dotnet/blob/master/playground/worker/README.md) shows a hosted event-bus subscription and an owned server's failure exit in a Generic Host.
- [AotCli](https://github.com/opencode-dotnet/opencode-sdk-dotnet/blob/master/playground/aotcli/README.md) inspects a repository's branch, changed files, top-level entries and config sources as a Native AOT console tool.

### 📋 Important Notes

- **From `1.0.0`, a version's parts say where a change comes from.** A patch (`1.0.x`) carries fixes
  and additive changes of the SDK's own. A minor (`1.x.0`) moves the pinned opencode release and may
  change the generated protocol models the way upstream changed them; its section here lists each
  such change. Only a major (`2.0.0`) breaks the hand-written surface. A family upstream marks
  experimental carries `[Experimental]` and may change in any minor.
- `1.0.0` is built on the go-live .NET 11 release-candidate SDK, a one-time exception to the GA-SDK
  rule; `1.0.1` rebuilds it on the GA SDK with no API change.

## [0.9.0-preview.15] - 2026-11-01

**The SDK speaks opencode 2.2.x and allocates much less.** The pinned server moves from 2.1.4 to
2.2.5. That moves the session log to `ExperimentalClient`, changes several generated protocol models
(listed below), and adds experimental schedules, artifacts, image and decision generation, usage
limits and file watching, a `types` filter on the event stream, and renaming of persistent terminals.
Open enums become generated extensible enums. On .NET 10, a prompt's event stream allocates about a
third less per frame, a one-shot call up to about a quarter less, and a 16 KiB terminal paste about 1 KB
instead of about 17 KB; the Performance section has the figures and the two trade-offs.

### 💥 Breaking changes

- **The upstream pin moves to opencode v2.2.5.** Most entries below follow a change upstream made
  between v2.1.4 and v2.2.5. The open-enum, `IMcp`, `savedPermissionId`, `OnStart` and `Optional<T>`
  entries are the SDK's own.
- **The session log moves to `ExperimentalClient.ReadSessionLogAsync`.** Upstream serves it as
  `experimental.session.log`, so `SessionClient.ReadLogAsync` is gone and `SessionLogRequest` is
  `ExperimentalSessionLogRequest`, with the same `After` and `Follow`. Migrate
  `client.Sessions.GetSessionClient(id).ReadLogAsync(new SessionLogRequest { … })` to
  `client.Experimental.ReadSessionLogAsync(id, new ExperimentalSessionLogRequest { … })`. The
  session-log types now carry `OPENCODE001`, the experimental client's diagnostic, and `OPENCODE003`
  is retired: a suppression of `OPENCODE003` becomes one of `OPENCODE001`.
- **`ExperimentalClient.SetVoiceSessionInstructionsAsync` is removed**, with
  `ExperimentalVoiceInstructionsRequest` and `ExperimentalVoiceInstructionsResponse`: upstream
  removed the operation.
- **`EventsClient.SubscribeAsync` takes an optional `EventSubscribeRequest` first.** Its `Types`
  limits the stream to the listed event types. A call that passed `requestOptions` by position
  names it instead: `SubscribeAsync(requestOptions: options)`.
- **Model variants have their own settings type.** `ModelVariant.Settings` is
  `ModelVariantSettings?` and `ConfigModelVariants.Settings` is `ConfigModelVariantSettings?`, as
  upstream separates a variant's settings from a model's.
- **`VoiceModel.Integration`, `VoiceModel.Workspace` and `ExperimentalVoiceSessionData.Session`
  are removed**, with `VoiceSessionReference`: upstream no longer declares them.
- **`ConfigInfoCompaction.Buffer` is `ConfigInfoCompactionBuffer?`, not `long?`.** Upstream now
  accepts a share of the context window such as `"20%"` besides a token count, so the value is a
  carrier: `Kind` says which arm it holds, `Text` the percentage and `WholeNumber` the token count.
  Migrate `config.Compaction.Buffer` to `buffer.WholeNumber` after checking
  `buffer.Kind == ConfigInfoCompactionBufferKind.WholeNumber`, and set it with
  `ConfigInfoCompactionBuffer.FromWholeNumber(...)` or `FromText("20%")`.
- **`PersistentPtyInfo.UserTitle` is required.** It is the title a user gave the terminal, or
  `null` when none was given; upstream always sends the key, so a terminal from a server that omits
  it no longer deserializes, and an initializer that builds a `PersistentPtyInfo` must set it.
- **`PersistentPtyUpdateRequest.Size` is optional (`PtySize?`), no longer required.** Code reading
  it must handle null before accessing its dimensions.
- **Open enums are generated extensible enums, not `string`.** A string enum beside a free string,
  such as a reasoning field's known names, now binds a generated extensible enum that carries any
  other value too. `ModelCompatibility.ReasoningField` and `ProviderCompatibility.ReasoningField`
  are `ModelReasoningField?`, `TuiCommandExecuteData.Command` is `TuiCommandName`,
  `ConfigWebSearchInfo.Provider` is `WebSearchProviderChoice`, and
  `SessionInstructionsUpdatedData.Delta`'s values are `SessionInstructionChange`.
  Migrate a comparison with `ModelReasoningField.ReasoningContent` (or the type's `Values` strings),
  and read the text with `ToString()`; nothing on the wire changes.
- **`IMcp` is now `IMcpServerConfig`, and `UnknownMcp` is now `UnknownMcpServerConfig`.**
  The union represents one MCP server's configuration, the value type of `Co
…[文件过长——仅保留首 16KB 与末 8KB]…
 request type and a generated response envelope; bound handles (`SessionClient`,
  `PtyClient`, `PersistentPtyClient`) partially apply a resource id over the shared pipeline.
- **Unions dispatch by tag, and tolerate what they do not know.** A discriminated union decodes by
  the literal tag the document declares. The live event stream additionally carries one
  prefix-tagged arm, so every `rpc.*` event dispatches to `EventRpc` — tried after the literal tags
  and before the carrier. Anything matching neither lands in that union's `Unknown*` variant with
  its tag and raw payload, so a server newer than the pinned snapshot widens an enumeration rather
  than breaking it.
- **A standalone server launcher.** `OpenCodeServer.StartAsync()` starts, monitors, and stops a
  private `opencode2 serve` child — generated lease credential, stdin-EOF ownership, bounded tree
  termination — and `CreateClient()` hands back a client already bound to it. An optional
  `OpenCodeServerOutput` collector, supplied through `OpenCodeServerOptions.Output`, retains a
  bounded tail of the child's stdout and stderr for pull snapshots that report truncation, and it
  stays readable after a failed start; `ProcessId` stays readable after disposal for the same
  diagnostic use. Real-process lifecycle acceptance runs on Windows, Linux, and macOS.
- **Server-sent event streaming.** `EventsClient.SubscribeAsync` follows the global bus and
  `SessionClient.GetLogAsync` follows one session's log, both as `IAsyncEnumerable<T>` of typed
  frames over the same transport, decoration, and status walls as one-shot calls. A body cut
  mid-event is reported rather than dispatched, and the contract's mid-stream failure channel
  surfaces as a typed exception instead of being discarded.
- **PTY and persistent-PTY terminal sessions.** `PtySession` and `PersistentPtySession` are
  hand-written WebSocket doors over a shared, family-neutral socket core: read frames, write input,
  dispose to close. The persistent family adds attach/handoff/snapshot semantics, byte-typed
  output and checkpoints, and the framed input protocol with viewport tracking.
- **Terminal connection lifetime a caller can drive.** A connection-owned receiver assembles
  frames into an internal queue independently of the caller's enumeration, so canceling a read ends
  only that wait: the same healthy connection can be read again, or written to, afterwards. Both
  connect options gained an init-only `SendTimeout` (default 30 seconds) bounding each input or
  resize send end to end, including the wait for the send gate. Connection termination delivers the
  frames it already holds before reporting its outcome, while disposal abandons unread frames and
  joins the connection's own work. A persistent PTY keeps its locally requested viewport coherent
  with the input it labels, rather than letting an inbound resize report overwrite it. See
  [the terminals guide](docs/guide/terminals.md#-cancellation-deadlines-and-disposal).
- **Dependency injection through `OpenCodeAI.Sdk.Extensions`.** `AddOpenCode(Action<…>)` or
  `AddOpenCode(IConfiguration)` registers one singleton client owning its transport for the
  container's lifetime, plus every sub-client resolved from that same instance — inject
  `SessionsClient` or `EventsClient` directly.
- **A typed error model.** Calls throw typed exceptions by default; `OpenCodeRequestOptions.NoThrow`
  returns the failure as data on the same envelope (`IsError`, `Error`) for the cases where a
  non-2xx is a normal answer. Transport failures map to their own exception family.
- **Cursor-based asynchronous pagination.** The two cursor-carrying list envelopes — session list
  and message list — expose the wire cursor directly, and `SessionClient.EnumerateMessagesAsync`
  follows it to exhaustion as an `IAsyncEnumerable<T>`.
- **Source-generated JSON.** `System.Text.Json` source generation throughout, with no reflection
  fallback anywhere in the serialization path. Both packages declare `IsAotCompatible` on
  `net10.0`; the one reflective seam, `AddOpenCode(IConfiguration)`, is annotated
  `[RequiresDynamicCode]` / `[RequiresUnreferencedCode]` so a trimmed or AOT build is warned rather
  than surprised.

### 🛠️ General

- **Target frameworks:** `netstandard2.0`, `net472`, `net8.0`, `net9.0`, `net10.0` — for both
  packages. The suite runs on `net472` on Windows, real-process launcher tests included, and on
  `net8.0`/`net9.0`/`net10.0` on all three OSes. `netstandard2.0` is a consumption target rather
  than a test target — it has no runtime to execute on, and the `net472` leg is what exercises its
  compile surface.
- **Protocol identity:** built against an accepted OpenAPI snapshot of upstream's `v2` branch, not
  a live branch. The exact commit, its digest, and the receipt-governed refresh procedure live in
  [`spec/SNAPSHOT.md`](spec/SNAPSHOT.md).
- **Generated output is committed and reviewed as source**, locked by a public-API baseline and
  verified by regeneration, so a protocol refresh arrives as a readable diff.
- **Test suite:** 5,138 tests green on Windows — the fullest leg, and the only one that adds the
  `net472` assemblies. Linux and macOS run the same suite on the three modern targets.

### 📋 Important Notes

- **Unofficial.** This project is not affiliated with or endorsed by the opencode team.
- **Three operations are declined by decision, not by omission.** `v2.config.get` and
  `v2.experimental.migration.v1.status` hit an undiscriminated object-union wall; `v2.fs.read` is
  a framework wildcard route with no OpenAPI path template to bind. Admitting any of them would
  mean inventing a contract upstream does not declare. See
  [API Coverage](README.md#-api-coverage).
- **Two operations are transport-owned, not missing.** `v2.pty.connect` and
  `v2.persistentPty.connect` are WebSocket upgrades, so they are served by the hand-written
  `PtySession` / `PersistentPtySession` doors rather than by generated code — fully usable, just
  not generated.
- **Pre-1.0 API.** The public surface is locked by a reviewed baseline, but it may still move
  before `1.0.0`. Breaking changes will be called out here with impact and migration path.

# opencode SDK for .NET

Typed .NET client for the opencode HTTP API; an MCP server built on it lives in a sibling
repository. The domain is
largely upstream's — opencode's concepts seen through an SDK lens — with a few terms this
project coins for itself.

## Language

### Upstream domain (as visible at the API surface)

**Session**:
A persistent conversation with an Agent; the API's central concept.

**Session metadata**:
Host-supplied annotations on a Session: arbitrary keys, JSON values, opaque to opencode, durable
from creation. Children and forks inherit the parent's unless the creator supplies its own. The
pinned document types it only as an object.

**Message**:
One entry in a Session's projected history; a discriminated union keyed by a literal `type` marker
(user, assistant, synthetic, system, skill, shell, compaction, idle, and the agent/model/location
selection records). Only an assistant Message carries a content list; the rest are flat. An idle
Message marks where a turn ended and carries the turn's outcome.

**Assistant content**:
A typed fragment of an assistant Message (text, reasoning, tool); a discriminated union keyed by a
literal `type` marker, carried in that Message's `content` list. No other Message kind has one.
_Avoid_: part (the retired 1.x term; survives only as a legacy `partID` on a revert record)

**Session inbox**:
The queue of pending work for one Session — a prompt, a synthetic message, a compaction, or a move
— each item either queued behind the current turn or steered into it.

**Compaction**:
The summarize-and-truncate boundary in a Session's history. It appears as its own Message kind,
and a Session's active context is the Messages after the last one.

**Event**:
Something that happened: an identified, typed record carrying its own `data` and, optionally, the
Location it happened in. Every Event is either durable or ephemeral.

**Durable / ephemeral Event**:
The two durability classes every Event belongs to. A durable Event carries an envelope naming its
Aggregate, its sequence in that Aggregate's log, and the schema version that committed it, so it
can be read back later; an ephemeral Event carries none and exists only for subscribers attached
at the time. In the SDK the envelope is `IDurableEnvelope`, which every durable Event's own
envelope record implements and which `ISessionEventDurable.Durable` returns.

**Aggregate**:
The unit a durable Event log is kept per: an id read from a named field of the Event's own `data`,
plus a monotonic sequence over the Events committed against it. Session Events aggregate on their
Session; others aggregate elsewhere, such as worktree resolution on its Project.

**Durable Session event stream**:
One Session Aggregate's durable Event log, read back over SSE. `after` is an exclusive sequence
taken from a durable envelope or a sync marker, `follow` continues into live Events, and a single
`log.synced` marker separates replay from live. The sequence is not contiguous and the log has no
retention policy. Replay and follow both read persisted Events, and persistence is a server option
that is off by default; without it, both deliver the marker alone.
_Avoid_: session events (ambiguous with the live stream)

**Live event stream**:
The instance-wide event stream; `EventSubscribeRequest.Types` filters by event type, with the initial
`server.connected` Event always included. The operation has no cursor, replay, or resume
channel, and is volatile by contract — a slow consumer overflows and fails the stream, and Events
during a disconnection are missed. Every connection opens with a synthetic `server.connected`
Event. The SDK reconnects the stream itself; a `server.connected` after the first means Events were
missed and authoritative state should be refreshed, and a stream that cannot reconnect for one
minute gives up and throws.

**Permission**:
The gate on agent actions, expressed as rules matching an action and a resource to an effect —
allow, deny, or ask. An `ask` raises a permission request answered through the API, and an answer
may be kept as a standing Project-scoped grant. Every Agent carries its own ruleset, and so does
every Session: a Session's ruleset is set at creation, replaced wholesale through `session.update`
with its Permissions member, evaluated after the Agent's rules with the last matching rule winning, and each
replacement raises the durable `session.permissions` Event.

**Form**:
A structured question the server raises and a client answers — typed fields, optional visibility
conditions, and a state that ends answered or cancelled. Raised against a Session or a Location.

**Integration**:
A connectable upstream service and the authentication methods it offers — API key, OAuth, a
command, or the environment. Connecting runs as an attempt with its own status and leaves a
connection behind; a Provider names the Integration it is connected through.

**Provider**:
An LLM provider entry in its own catalog, carrying activation state and request settings — not its
Models, which form a separate catalog. A Provider names the Integration it is connected through.

**Model**:
One entry in the model catalog, naming the Provider it belongs to and carrying its capabilities,
variants, costs, and limits. A Model carries two ids: its **catalog id**, the identity within this
catalog, and its **provider model id**, the identity the Provider's own API uses. Sessions, Agents,
and Messages reference a Model by catalog id, provider, and optional variant rather than embedding
the entry; the provider model id never appears in a reference.
_Avoid_: model id alone (it is ambiguous between the two).

**Agent**:
A configured opencode persona — `build` by default, others from config or plugins — selectable per
Session or attachable to a single prompt. Carries its own Permission ruleset, an optional Model,
and a step budget.
_Avoid_: mode (an Agent's `mode` is its primary/subagent eligibility, not its persona)

**Server process**:
One running `opencode serve` process (one endpoint); the API is bound to a single Server
process, and cross-process aggregation lives above the SDK. Owns process-global state (auth store,
the live event stream and the durable Event log, Sessions, Projects, saved
Permissions). Configuration is not among them; it belongs to the Instance.

**Location**:
Public HTTP addressing by absolute directory. Resolving one yields its Project. Core and some
event/log schemas retain workspace fields; those are distinct contracts, not an HTTP selector.

**Project**:
The repository root a Location resolves to, carrying its own id and canonical path. Sessions,
saved Permissions, and worktrees are scoped to it.

**Worktree**:
A managed local directory in a Project's worktree inventory. Create, list, remove, and refresh take an explicit projectID. A caller can resolve that ID through
`location.get` for its directory. Creation optionally names a parent directory and a child name.

**Worktree strategy**:
A server-registered strategy used to discover and create Worktrees. The canonical Project
selects a registered strategy for creation; removal uses the recorded strategy. The SDK does not define a closed
strategy list or choose server defaults.

**Workspace**:
An upstream core addressing concept retained in some event/log contracts. The pinned public HTTP
API exposes neither workspace lifecycle operations nor workspace request targeting.

**Instance**:
One Location's working context inside a Server process — its configuration, agents, tools, and MCP
servers — selected per request via Directory targeting; a Server process hosts many, keyed by
Location. The Project is resolved from the Location, not chosen alongside it.

**Directory targeting**:
Per-request Location targeting via `location[...]` query parameters, with the
`x-opencode-directory` header as the ambient channel the server resolves
after an explicit directory query value; an unset directory falls back to the server's own working
directory.

**PTY**:
A pseudo-terminal session managed through the API.

**PTY connection**:
The live WebSocket attached to one PTY, carrying replayed and live output out and input in.
Distinct from the PTY itself, which outlives any connection to it.

**Replay cursor**:
The absolute position in a PTY's retained output. Normal PTY: a connection omitting it replays the
whole retained buffer, `-1` attaches live-only, and a value at or above zero resumes from there.
Persistent PTY: omitted means 0 (the oldest retained byte), there is no live-only mode, and the
resume anchors are `replay_complete.endOffset` and `Info.Output.Tail`.

**Connect ticket**:
The short-lived, single-use credential the token door mints for handing a PTY connection to a
browser. The SDK never mints one for its own connection.

**Persistent PTY**:
A terminal owned by the `opencode-pty` daemon rather than by the Server process; it survives a
server restart through a handoff, is keyed to a Session, and is the source of `read`'s "current
terminal".

**Handoff**:
The expiring, single-use ticket that transfers ownership of the `opencode-pty` daemon from an
outgoing Server process to its replacement, which must claim it before becoming ready. Its
`instanceID` identifies the daemon process, not an Instance.

**Attachment**:
One live connection to a Persistent PTY: its identity, its controller/observer role, the resize
generation it attached at, and the replay bounds the server granted it.
_Avoid_: attachment (unqualified — the `*Attachment` types on the surface are prompt attachments:
files, agents, and skills carried on a Message)

**Controller / Observer**:
The two roles a Persistent PTY grants an Attachment. A Controller writes input and resizes; an
Observer reads output only, and its input is dropped server-side. The server grants the role, so
it is not necessarily the one the connection asked for.

**Checkpoint**:
The terminal-escape byte stream that repaints a screen state, carried base64 on the wire and as
bytes in the SDK.

**Framed input**:
The `input_protocol=1` layout a Persistent PTY connection writes: `[type][cols][rows][data]`, so
every input or control message carries the viewport it was typed at.

### This project's language

**Protocol surface** (historically "modern surface" in dated research docs):
The pinned protocol API document — the surface this SDK generates (ADR-0005). Operation IDs
are prefixless at the pin; public names carry no protocol-version prefix.
_Avoid_: v2, V2 (in public naming); legacy (the retired 1.x dual-surface vocabulary)

**Launcher**:
The in-core component that starts, monitors, and stops a local `opencode serve` process —
`OpenCodeServer.StartAsync` and its working object, covering the standalone-server connection
mode. Discovery/attachment of background services is deliberately not the launcher's job; those
are `OpenCodeServer`'s other modes.

**Standalone server**:
A fresh private `opencode serve --stdio --port 0` child owned by the SDK caller through
`OpenCodeServer`: generated lease credential, stdin-EOF ownership, bounded tree termination.
Upstream's `Standalone.start` connection mode.

**Background service**:
Upstream's registered daemon connection mode (`Service.discover/ensure/stop` over a
registration file); in the SDK, `OpenCodeServer.DiscoverAsync`, `OpenCodeServer.EnsureAsync`,
and `OpenCodeServer.StopAsync`.

**Registration file**:
The on-disk record a background service publishes (address, credential, instance identity) so
clients can discover it; an upstream-observed contract outside the OpenAPI pin. Its identity is
the four fields upstream's `same()` compares — `id`, `version`, `url`, `pid` — never the password.

**Process identity**:
The pid together with the start time the operating system recorded for the process. The token
`StopAsync` compares immediately before every signal and at every look of its poll, so a pid the
operating system reused for an unrelated process is never signalled and reads as the registered
process being gone. Distinct from the registration file's identity, which names a service, not a
process.

**Registered server handle**:
A non-owning `OpenCodeServer` produced by discovery or Ensure: `OwnsProcess` is false
and disposal never stops the shared service.
_Avoid_: guarded server handle, shared handle (draft names for the same thing)

**Service channel**:
The CLI's compiled release identity that selects the registration and service-config filenames and
the legacy-migration rules; the release channels share `service.json`, `local` and custom channels
use distinct names. The SDK has none compiled in: a caller may name one, and the null default reads
the shared release registration.

**Accepted snapshot**:
The reviewed protocol identity the SDK builds against: an exact upstream commit, the committed
`spec/openapi.json` digest, an ordered snapshot recipe, a sorted operation-set digest, and the
matching submodule gitlink. Provenance in `spec/SNAPSHOT.md`.
_Avoid_: spec pin (retired term)

**Snapshot recipe**:
The ordered procedure producing the accepted document from the exact upstream commit: upstream's
own pinned generator, run over a patch list that is normally empty. Upstream's committed document
is never the input.

**Snapshot receipt**:
The immutable record of one prepared snapshot candidate — inputs, hashes, patches, invariants —
reviewed by a human before it is applied.

**Restore patch**:
A temporary, hash-verified snapshot-production patch recovering contract content upstream's
projection lost; carries an upstream report and a retirement predicate.

**Source watch**:
The pinned set of upstream files a hand-written door reads as inputs — each a watched source
recorded by path, SHA-256 blob hash, and one content anchor in `spec/source-watch.json` and the
receipt's `watchedSources`. A refresh-time review trigger only; it never reaches ingestion,
curation, or emission.

**Contract inventory**:
The complete operation set of the accepted document, each operation carrying its admission state
(selected, pending, declined, or transport-owned).

**Target surface**:
The operations required to be callable; defaults to the complete contract inventory.

**Transport-owned operation**:
An operation whose transport the HTTP pipeline cannot carry (a WebSocket upgrade);
generator-owned as inventory and exclusion fingerprint, callable only through a hand-written
door.

**Operation-identity row**:
A reason-bearing curation row admitting and naming an operation whose upstream identity violates
upstream's own conventions; carries the upstream report and retires when the fix lands.

**Naming grammar**:
The closed set of identifier segments (`create`, `get`, `list`, `remove`, `rename`, `timeout`,
`update`) that name an operation's verb when they close its identity. A `GET` without one reads
as `Get<Subject>Async`; any other operation without one has no mechanical name and needs an
operation-name row. The HTTP method is never a name source.

**Operation-name row**:
A reason-bearing curation row naming an operation the naming grammar cannot name, or names
gracelessly; the binder validates the identifier and every collision.

**Enum member-name row**:
A reason-bearing curation row naming the C# member one enum value becomes where the mechanical
casing is graceless (`2026-07-28` → `Revision20260728`, not `Value20260728`).

**Parameter-name row**:
A reason-bearing curation row naming the C# parameter one route value becomes where the mechanical
name says less than the rest of the surface (`shell.get`'s `id` → `shellId`); the wire name still
fills the route.

**Model layer**:
The generated types and serializer registry shipped inside `OpenCode.Sdk`.

**Envelope**:
The generated, typed per-operation response object carrying status/error state plus named
payload properties.

**Single-key envelope**:
A success body an operation declares inline as an object requiring exactly one property that is
not `data` (`SpecEnvelopeShape.SingleKey`); the payload flattens onto the response under that
key's PascalCase name and the wrapper is never emitted as a model. An inline object whose sole
property is optional has no payload the envelope can promise and refuses at bind time instead.

**Bound handle**:
A sub-client bound to one resource id (e.g. a session) — partial application over the
shared pipeline; never caches server state.

**Cursor sequence** (`CursorSequence<TPage, TItem>`):
The value a generated `Enumerate*Async` companion returns. It enumerates as the items of every page
in order and exposes the same traversal's page envelopes through `Pages`. It is a recipe rather than
a buffer: each enumeration issues its own requests.

**PTY session** (`PtySession`):
The working object over one PTY connection: read frames, write input, dispose to close. One of the
two doors that build their own transport instead of riding the HTTP pipeline (the persistent PTY
session is the other).

**PTY frame**:
One message read from a PTY connection — either output text or the single cursor control frame
the server sends once the retained buffer has been replayed.

**Terminal socket core**:
The family-neutral WebSocket lifecycle both PTY sessions share — receive and reassembly,
serialized sends, bounded close, disposal — with per-family decode, close, and upgrade-failure
behavior behind named seams.

**Connection snapshot**:
The construction-time endpoint, credential, and ambient location the pipeline publishes for a
door that cannot ride its policies.

**Curation config**:
The generator's declarative, fail-closed input mapping spec constructs to public names and
rules; an unmapped construct breaks generation.

**Stabilize-duplicate collapse**:
The mechanical fold of a reachable `<base>_<N>` component into `<base>` when
`StabilizeDuplicatePolicy` finds the two structurally identical, refusing by name when it does
not; recorded as an implicit alias in `.generated-manifest.json`'s `implicitAliases` section
rather than a curated `schemaAliases` row.

**Prefix-tagged arm**:
The at-most-one branch of a tagged union whose discriminator is a string prefix — Effect's
`TemplateLiteral` projected as `^<prefix>[\s\S]*?$` — rather than a literal; `rpc.*` events on the
live event stream. Dispatch tries literal tags, then the prefix, then the Unknown variant carrier.
_Avoid_: pattern arm (a general regex is never admitted); catch-all (the Unknown variant carrier is
the catch-all).

**Unknown variant carrier**:
The per-union `Unknown*` variant preserving a tag string and raw payload for an unrecognized
discriminator. On the live event stream and durable Session event stream, it can also hold a known
variant that cannot be read; the union's prefix-tagged arm still excludes its markers from the carrier
([stream payload tolerance](docs/architecture/client-runtime.md#server-sent-events)).

**Plugin activation**:
The asynchronous per-Location settling of a server's plugins, during which Providers register, the
model catalog fills, and the VCS summary learns its provider. The pinned HTTP API has no activation
barrier. An info answer proves process liveness only; a catalog read can observe an empty or
partial registry, and a VCS summary without a provider has not settled yet. Consumers that require
a particular registration wait for that identity under a bounded cancellation token.
_Avoid_: readiness (that is the launcher's stdout contract, a different thing).

**Hoisted member**:
A property a generated union interface declares because every member of that union already
declares it in the same shape — the same wire name, required-ness, nullability, and represented
type, ignoring a literal value that discriminates nothing. It is nullable on the interface
because the union's unknown carrier materializes none of them, and it is never the discriminator.
Where each member promotes its own record for one identical shape, the hoisted member's type is a
generated **carrier interface** those records implement; the records keep their own identity.
_Avoid_: shared member (ambiguous with a property two unrelated schemas happen to share)

**Plugin RPC**:
A method surface a server-side plugin registers under an `rpcID`; `rpc.call` dispatches one
`method` to it at a Location with an untyped JSON `input` and returns an untyped `output`, and the
plugin's notifications ride the live event stream as `rpc.*` events (the prefix-tagged arm).
_Avoid_: RPC alone (the SDK's own HTTP calls are not RPC).

**Fingerprint pin**:
The committed hash of an excluded operation's own spec subtree, which names the components it
references; CI breaks when the pinned construct drifts.

**Output manifest**:
The committed inventory of generated files; generated-ness is tracked here, never by
folder or file-name convention.

**Recorded tolerance**:
An explicit, registered runtime exception to the fail-closed default.

**Behavior core**:
The hand-written transport core where all request behavior lives; generated methods only
delegate to it.
